wv_junkyard_wall.blurb: A short, busy wall just off the road near the New River Gorge Bridge, inside the national park. Nearly all of the 40 or so climbs are trad, with a couple of top-rope lines and a lone sport route, spanning easy 5.6 and 5.7 up through a big cluster of 5.10 and 5.11 and a few 5.12s. Routes run roughly 50 to 65 feet. Because the walk is minimal and the campground is close, expect crowds, guided groups and kids; share lines and remember a rope hung on a route does not hold it for you. Anchors are easy to reach from above, so many lines get top-roped. Bring a rack if you plan to lead. Drones are prohibited.

wv_01_sandstonia.blurb: Sandstonia, also called Bubba City, is a long sandstone wall north of the New River Gorge Bridge near Fayetteville, beside the national park. Our catalog lists mostly sport climbs with a handful of trad lines, running from about 5.6 to 5.12 with the bulk in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. Closely spaced bolts and plenty of moderates make it popular, and weekends can get very crowded. Access has historically crossed private land along the roadside; a land trust now owns the gateway property and plans parking and trails, but no lot existed yet when it announced the purchase, so check current local info before you drive out.
